gaps.text: In-line measurement of Process temperature with temperature sensor

Combining several spectroscopy methods (data fusion) (Low-level fusion: Raman and UV/Vis spectra synchronised to a common time step and merged into one augmented matrix, with block scaling so neither method dominates. Both probes must sample the same well-mixed broth volume at the same time. Each method keeps its own calibration against its own reference data, and the fused model must beat the best single method on held-out runs or it is dropped.)
Sterilisation, cleaning-in-place and fouling behaviour of the probes in a fermentation environment are not covered by the supplied material.
Detection limits for specific metabolites in this yeast broth are not stated in the sources and must come from the feasibility trials.

items.finding: Low-level data fusion rearranges data into a new matrix by placing variables from different sources one after the other.
items.how_it_applies: This supports the low-level data fusion approach by showing how the combined matrix can be structured, though model complementarity should be evaluated first.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The cited study discusses food analytics rather than yeast fermentation, so the data structure and complementarity might not transfer directly.

citation.quote: Low-level data fusion (LLDF) is considered the simplest method to achieve a combination of inputs. In this case, the data is rearranged into a new data matrix, where the variables coming from different sources are placed one after the other.
citation.label: E03 ¶31

items.finding: Probe housings must be compatible with the installation environment, process chemistry, and sterilization and cleaning protocols across scales.
items.how_it_applies: This highlights the need to test probe materials against the specific sterilization and cleaning procedures used in the fermentation environment.
items.limits_and_transfer_risks: The source discusses biopharmaceutical manufacturing generally rather than the specific yeast fermentation broth of this enquiry.
